summary.intent: Execute all 9 plans in Phase 66 ('API Schema Cutover, Publish Gate & Tombstone') using wave-based parallel execution with subagents in isolated git worktrees, advancing the API from a legacy share_keys/folder_ipns model to a descriptor-ref/IpnsRecord node/v3 model.
summary.outcome: Completed Waves 1–3 (6 of 9 plans: 66-01 through 66-06). API build is green (exit 0), full API test suite passes (767/0), and the regenerated API client (109 files) reflects the new surface. Waves 4–5 (66-07, 66-08, 66-09) were not yet started at transcript end.

repo: worktree-safety.cjs deletion guard is unconditional — no override flag exists; any branch that deletes files requires manual verification and merge, bypassing the cleanup helper entirely.
worktree.baseRef='head' means worktrees fork from live HEAD, so inter-wave merges do not cause base-mismatch halts in subsequent waves.
pnpm install --prefer-offline inside a worktree does not build @cipherbox/crypto — the dist/ directory is absent and must be built explicitly before ipns module resolution works.

api:generate builds the OpenAPI doc in-process (no live DB or server required), but its trailing pnpm lint:fix runs repo-wide — it will exit non-zero if Wave 4 packages (web, sdk-core) are still broken.
66-02's plan explicitly defers behavioral proof (upsertIpnsRecord) to the sdk-e2e suite in 66-09; ipns.service.spec.ts was intentionally excluded from 66-02's files_modified scope.

The API build is intentionally red between Wave 1 and Wave 2 by design — type foundations (66-01/66-03) land before logic rewrites (66-02/66-04); the post-merge gate should be targeted, not a full monorepo build.
Parallel git worktree add calls cause .git/config.lock races; worktrees must be added sequentially even when executors run in parallel.

code.finding: Had orphaned ShareKey import (line 32) and entity registration (line 98) after 66-03 deleted share-key.entity.ts — neither 66-01 nor 66-04 covered this; orchestrator fixed it as a post-merge cross-plan gap.
Also imported the deleted ShareKey entity — a second orphan from 66-03's deletion discovered when 66-06 ran api:generate; executor applied Rule 3 auto-fix.

28 tests were stale against 66-02's atomic-CAS rewrite: mocks only had findOne/save, lacking createQueryBuilder. All 28 were adapted (not deleted) by adding a chainable createQueryBuilder mock with mockQbExecute override per test.

workflow: When a service's repository access pattern changes fundamentally (findOne+save → createQueryBuilder+update), existing unit tests need mock adaptation, not deletion — behavioral coverage should be preserved.

Post-merge test gates for intermediate waves should target only the packages changed in that wave (e.g., pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api test) rather than the full monorepo, to avoid blocking on known downstream breakage that later waves will fix.

Orphaned import sites (module registrations, script imports) are a predictable cross-plan gap when entity files are deleted; a grep for the deleted symbol name across the repo should be part of any deletion plan's acceptance criteria.
The GSD orchestrator pattern of fixing post-merge cross-plan gaps directly (rather than creating a new gap-closure plan) is sanctioned and efficient for single-file orphans.
Dispatching worktree executors in separate sequential messages (not parallel tool calls) prevents git config lock races during worktree setup, even when the executors themselves run in parallel.

friction: worktree-safety.cjs deletion guard has no override flag — required manual branch inspection and merge for both Wave 1 (66-03: 3 deleted files) and Wave 2 (66-04: 5 deleted spec files), each time abandoning the cleanup helper entirely.

app.module.ts and generate-openapi.ts were orphaned by 66-03's ShareKey deletion but not in any plan's files_modified — discovered only at post-merge build time, adding an unplanned orchestrator fix step.

28 ipns.service.spec.ts tests failed post-merge because 66-02 deliberately excluded them from scope — required dispatching an additional alignment subagent before the Wave 2 gate could pass, adding ~16 min of unplanned serial work.
pnpm install --prefer-offline in worktrees silently omits crypto dist/ build, causing module resolution failures deep in the executor run rather than at setup time.
api:generate's repo-wide lint:fix step makes Wave 3 execution fragile while Wave 4 packages are still broken — executor had to work around this rather than running the script cleanly end-to-end.
